title: 3 Nights in Kuala Lumpur — A Couple's Cultural & Foodie Itinerary: Durian Farms, Street Food & Temples
description: A personalized 3-night Kuala Lumpur itinerary for a couple — durian farm day trip, Jalan Alor street food, Batu Caves, Petronas Towers, and the best nasi lemak in Malaysia.

days.title: Arrive, Check In & Eat Everything on Jalan Alor
days.description: Your first day is all about settling in and letting KL's street food scene blow your minds. No monuments, no museums — just wander, eat, repeat. The food here is absurdly good and absurdly cheap. Pace yourselves, because tomorrow involves durian.

activities.name: KLIA → Bukit Bintang
activities.description: FromKLIA/KLIA2: Take the KLIA Ekspres to KL Sentral (~30 min, RM55/person), then monorail to Bukit Bintang (10 min). Or grab a Grab car directly to your hotel (~RM80–120, 1 hour depending on traffic). Drop bags and freshen up.
tips: Stay in the Bukit Bintang area — it's the sweet spot for food, transit, and nightlife. Excellent mid-range options: The Face Suites (serviced apartments with KLCC views), Tian Jing Hotel (boutique, great value), or Invito Hotel (walkable to everything). Budget around RM250–500/night for a comfortable couple's stay.

activities.name: Petaling Street & Chinatown
activities.description: Walk through KL's Chinatown as the evening energy picks up. Petaling Street is a bustling night market with vendors, street food, and trinkets. But the real draw is the food on the surrounding streets — this is where Malay, Chinese, and Indian cuisines collide in beautiful ways.

activities.name: Jalan Alor Street Food Crawl
activities.description: This is it — Southeast Asia's most famous food street and your dinner destination. The entire road closes to traffic at night and fills with tables, smoke from grills, and hundreds of people eating their hearts out. Walk the full length first, then double back to hit the spots that caught your eye.

days.title: Durian Farm Day Trip — The King of Fruits Awaits
days.description: Today's the day you asked for. The drive to Bentong/Raub takes you through gorgeous Malaysian highlands to the heartland of Musang King durian production. April is prime durian season — the trees will be heavy with fruit. This is a full day trip, and it's absolutely worth it.

activities.name: KL → Bentong (2–2.5 hours)
activities.description: Leave by8:00 AMto beat the heat and make the most of the day. Best options: Option A — Private driver:Book through your hotel or Grab. A full-day return trip costs RM250–350. This is the most comfortable option and lets you stop wherever you want.
tips: The drive through Karak Highway and Bentong's winding mountain roads is beautiful — lush tropical rainforest, palm oil plantations, and misty hills. Stop at Bentong town for a pit stop and fresh soy milk from the famous Kow Po coffee shop.

activities.name: Musang King Durian Farm Experience
activities.description: The Raub/Bentong region produces Malaysia's finest Musang King durians (also called Mao Shan Wang). At a farm visit, you'll walk through durian orchards, learn about how trees are grafted and cultivated, and understand why Musang King commands premium prices worldwide. Then comes the best part:eating freshly fallen durian right at the farm. Durian is best within hours of dropping from the tree — the flesh is creamy, bittersweet, and nothing like the frozen stuff you get overseas. The farm will crack open fruit after fruit for you to taste different varieties.

activities.name: Chamang Waterfall or Hot Springs
activities.description: If you have energy after the durian feast (you might not — durian is filling), two excellent stops near Bentong: Chamang Waterfall— A stunning multi-tiered waterfall 15 minutes from Bentong town. Cool off in the natural pools. Bring swimwear and water shoes. The jungle setting is gorgeous.
details: 📍 Chamang: Jalan Chamang, Bentong · Free · Best before 16:00

activities.name: Drive Back & Bangsar Dinner
activities.description: Head back to KL (2–2.5 hours). You'll arrive around 6–7 PM, perfect for dinner in Bangsar — KL's trendiest food neighborhood.

days.neighborhoods: Batu Caves · KLCC · Merdeka Square · Jalan Alor
days.title: Batu Caves, Petronas Towers & One Last Night Market
days.description: Your biggest sightseeing day — but we've paced it so you're never rushing. Batu Caves in the cool morning, culture and art midday, Petronas Towers at golden hour, and one last glorious food crawl to send you off.

activities.name: Batu Caves
activities.description: Get there by8:00 AMbefore the heat and tour buses arrive. Take the KTM Komuter from KL Sentral to Batu Caves station (30 min, RM2.60) or Grab (~RM25). The 272 rainbow-painted stairs lead up to a massive limestone cave housing Hindu shrines. The 43-meter golden statue of Lord Murugan at the base is staggering. Inside the main Temple Cave, shafts of light pierce through holes in the limestone ceiling — genuinely awe-inspiring. The Dark Cave eco-tour (RM35, 45 min) is excellent if you want to learn about the cave's unique ecosystem.
details: 📍 Gombak, Selangor · Free (Dark Cave RM35) · Opens 6:00 · 30 min from KL Sentral

activities.name: Merdeka Square & Colonial KL
activities.description: Head to Merdeka Square (Dataran Merdeka) — where Malaysian independence was declared in 1957. The massive flagpole, the beautiful Sultan Abdul Samad Building (Moorish architecture), and the surrounding colonial-era buildings give you a sense of KL's layered history — Malay sultanates, British colonialism, and modern independence. Walk through to theCentral Market (Pasar Seni)— an Art Deco building from 1888, now filled with Malaysian arts, crafts, batik, pewter, and souvenirs. Great for picking up gifts. The batik workshops on the upper floor are worth a look.
details: 📍 Jalan Raja, KL · Free · Central Market 10:00–22:00

activities.name: Islamic Arts Museum Malaysia
activities.description: One of Southeast Asia's finest museums and a hidden gem most tourists skip. Stunning collections of Quran manuscripts, architectural models of famous mosques, Ottoman ceramics, jewelry, and textiles. The building itself is gorgeous — domed ceilings, intricate tilework, and peaceful galleries. The gift shop has beautiful Islamic geometric art prints and calligraphy. Spend 1–1.5 hours here. The air conditioning alone makes it worth the visit on a hot April day.
details: 📍 Jalan Lembah Perdana · RM20/person · 10:00–18:00 · Closed Mondays

activities.name: KLCC & Petronas Twin Towers
activities.description: Time it for5:00–7:00 PMfor golden hour views. The towers are magnificent at dusk when they're lit from within. Options: Skybridge + Observation Deck(RM80/person, book online in advance at petronastwintowers.com.my) — the 86th floor views are spectacular, especially at sunset. Book the 5:30 or 6:00 PM slot.
details: 📍 KLCC, Jalan Ampang · Park: Free / Skybridge: RM80 · Park closes 22:00

days.title: Morning Culture, Last Bites & Home
days.description: A gentle final morning. One more neighborhood, one more incredible meal, and you're off — carrying enough food memories to last until your next trip.

activities.name: Kampung Baru — KL's Malay Village Heart
activities.description: A 10-minute walk from KLCC, Kampung Baru feels like a different world — a traditional Malay village surrounded by skyscrapers. Wooden houses, fruit stalls, and some of the best Malay food in the city. It's the cultural soul of KL and most tourists never set foot here.

activities.time: 🕌 Late Morning — Masjid Jamek & River of Life
activities.name: Masjid Jamek & Confluence
activities.description: If time allows before your flight, visit Masjid Jamek — KL's oldest mosque (1909), beautifully situated at the confluence of the Klang and Gombak rivers (the spot where KL was literally founded). The surrounding River of Life project has turned the riverbanks into a pleasant waterfront walkway with blue-lit fountains at night.
details: 📍 Jalan Tun Perak · Free (modest dress required) · 8:30–12:30, 14:30–16:00

activities.name: Head to KLIA
activities.description: Allow 2 hours for airport transit. KLIA Ekspres from KL Sentral (30 min, RM55/person) or Grab (~RM80–120, 1 hour). If you have checked bags, the KLIA Ekspres also has a check-in counter at KL Sentral for some airlines.
tips: Last-minute durian fix? The duty-free shops at KLIA sell vacuum-packed Musang King durian — frozen and sealed, allowed on most airlines. It's not as good as farm-fresh, but it'll get you through until your next Malaysia trip. Also grab some kaya (coconut jam) and white coffee packets as souvenirs — they're lightweight and everyone loves them.

days.title: 💰 Budget Breakdown — For Two
days.description: KL is extraordinarily affordable. Here's what to expect for two people over 3 nights. All prices in USD (1 USD ≈ RM4.5).
